purpose: The orchestrator's decisions on the split proposals of combined Part II design jobs (PROTOCOL.md section 9). A design job given several Part II directions of one parent may plan one of them and propose the others as roadmaps of their own, in its packet's `restructure`. Each split listed here gives every roadmap in `roadmaps` a design job of its own, with the paper routes that name it (make_queue.paper_designs); the combined job keeps the rest. `after` lists the split-off roadmaps whose design a split-off design waits for, and `notes` adds to a split-off design's brief.

notes.EllipticCurveModularityImaginaryQuadrati: This is the main theorem of Caraiani and Newton. Two roadmaps are designed alongside it and supply its inputs: CrystallineLocalGlobalCompatibilityCM (P-ordinary degree shifting, crystalline local–global compatibility and Barsotti–Tate lifting, from the same paper) and EllipticCurveModularityPartIIGL2TypeAbelianVarieties (the Q-curve step). Import from them rather than planning those results here.
notes.EllipticCurveModularityPartIIGL2TypeAbel: It supplies the Q-curve step of EllipticCurveModularityImaginaryQuadratic, designed alongside it.
notes.EllipticCurveModularityWild3Adic: EllipticCurveModularity keeps its own proof of the same endpoint; this roadmap records the wild 3-adic route as a distinct proof, and nothing in EllipticCurveModularity depends on it.

notes.CrystallineLocalGlobalCompatibilityCM: It is the key new input of Caraiani and Newton. EllipticCurveModularityImaginaryQuadratic, designed alongside it from the same paper, builds on its lifting theorems.
notes.PotentialAutomorphyDworkMotivesPartII: It also owns the self-dual Dwork family and its monodromy, which PotentialAutomorphyInfrastructurePartII's PL.5/dwork-potential-ordinary-automorphy imports (a gap recorded in that packet).
notes.WeightZeroCrystallineAutomorphyLifting: CrystallineLocalGlobalCompatibilityCM is its prerequisite: build on that roadmap's design. The connects relation and potential diagonalizability it uses are owned by PotentialAutomorphyInfrastructurePartII (PL.1).
